score_meanings.promise_vocabulary: 0 drifts into claims/profiles/central trust-ledger framing, 5 stays promise-first and pCID-specific
score_meanings.simplicity_durability: 0 overbuilt or fragile, 5 minimal, durable, and small-device-friendly under the 100-year goal

promise_theory_rules: A promise is a scoped declaration of intent.
No agent can make a promise on behalf of another agent.
Trust is a local assessment of whether a promise will be kept.
Promises to receive or use are not equivalent to obligations, impositions, or promises to give.
promise_theory_references: Mark Burgess, In Search of Certainty
Mark Burgess, Promise Theory: Principles and Applications

assessment.rationale: Strong PT-clean restatement of nested signed payloads with explicit outer promise and local trust. It is less strong for this freeze/mutation scenario because it does not itself define lineage, freeze evidence, or supersession rules, so it only partially explains how post-freeze changes avoid mutating history.
strengths: Explicit outer promise improves PT correctness over implicit transport authority.
Clear outer/inner boundary helps audit what is being promised versus what is merely carried as evidence.
Small envelope plus pCID-typed nested payload supports durable, inspectable artifacts.
weaknesses: No explicit model for freeze evidence, supersession, or amendment lineage.
Scenario fit is partial because post-freeze mutation handling lives outside the envelope semantics.
Failure handling is mostly trust rejection, not explicit history-preserving mutation resolution.
risks: A receiver could misread a new signed payload as authority to mutate prior frozen state unless lineage rules are defined elsewhere.
Freeze and supersession semantics may leak into ad hoc application conventions instead of durable envelope-level evidence.
The nested signature may be over-trusted as global authority rather than one local input to trust assessment.
open_questions: How would freeze evidence be carried or referenced so a post-freeze mutation request is clearly evaluated as a new specimen or superseding pCID rather than a rewrite of history?
What local evidence distinguishes an allowed amendment from an invalid mutation against a frozen lineage?
Should the outer promise explicitly include lineage or supersession pointers for frozen artifacts?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.

autonomous_agents.note: The design keeps sender and receiver autonomy explicit.

scoped_intent.note: The outer-layer promise is narrowly scoped to parsing and interpretation of nested bytes.

no_promises_for_others.note: The sender promises only about the carried structure and evidence object, not on behalf of other agents.

no_guaranteed_outcomes.note: The envelope offers evidence and intent, not guaranteed interpretation or acceptance.

local_trust_assessment.note: Trust is explicitly receiver-local and based on sender promise plus nested signature evidence.

accept_use_not_obligation.note: Receivers decide locally whether to trust and use the envelope; acceptance is not framed as obligation.
